The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.text: Worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man Antiochus, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army. That is what noisome looks like in the record.
precepts.point: The key thing: the sore falls on the people that worship the image of the beast and have his mark. If it is only them, where are we? We are delivered.
precepts.why:
The first vial brings “a noisome and grievous sore.” Noisome means foul smelling, harmful, noxious, extremely offensive to the senses, particularly the smell: a real nasty sore. It is the same plague that came on ancient Egypt, a boil breaking forth upon man and upon beast throughout all the land.

The record shows what noisome looks like on a man. When the Lord struck the wicked king Antiochus, “the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man, and whiles he lived in sorrow and pain, his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” His flesh fell off him and his stink offended his whole army.

What could make a man get like that? A nuclear bomb explosion causes severe radiation burns, known as cutaneous radiation injury, that frequently lead to intense itching, blistering and open sores. The burns come in stages: first redness and swelling, then a latent phase, then severe blistering and deep, long lasting necrotic ulcers. When a nuclear bomb goes off and the blast does not kill you, you are going to be rotten, your skin falling off, and it is going to be noisome.

That is how we know this first plague belongs to that one hour, when the destruction comes on America, modern day Egypt: the same kind of sore that ate Antiochus alive falls on the men who have the mark of the beast.

precepts.text: Antiochus, swelling with anger and speaking proudly that he would make Jerusalem a burying place of the Jews, was smitten by the God of Israel with a remediless pain of the bowels as soon as he spoke, ceased not from bragging and breathing out fire against the Jews, fell from his chariot and was carried violently, and worms rose out of his body while his flesh fell away and the stench sickened his whole army.
precepts.point: The people shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut up burnt in the fire. Not the fire of 2 Kings: Isaiah 9:5, every battle of the warrior is with confused noise and garments rolled in blood, but this shall be with burning and fuel of fire, thermonuclear fire.
precepts.why:
“Now will I rise, saith the Lord; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself. Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath, as fire, shall devour you.” What does that mean, your breath as fire shall devour you? When you speak great words and talk big talk that you can't back up with God, you are going to eat your words. Like Nicanor pointing at the temple and saying we are going to tear it to the ground. Antiochus is the example.

“Then swelling with anger, he thought to avenge upon the Jews the disgrace done unto him by those that made him flee.” He commanded his chariotman to drive without ceasing, “the judgment of God now following him. For he had spoken proudly in this sort, That he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” He wanted to destroy us.

“But the Lord Almighty, the God of Isreal, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague.” As soon as he had spoken those words: that is what “your breath, as fire, shall devour you” means. “A pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts; And that most justly: for he had tormented other men’s bowels with many and strange torments.” Good for him.

“Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews.” There it is again, breathing out fire, the bottom of Isaiah 33:11: your big talk is going to burn you up. Then “he fell down from his chariot, carried violently”: he fell off the chariot and it dragged him. It was bad enough he had stomach pains; now his whole body hurt.

“And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, (so proud was he beyond the condition of man) and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground” … “So that the worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man” … “and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army.” He began to stink worse than shit; his whole army could smell him.

That is what is coming to the nations talking big right now. America breaks the covenant and regards no man, and Israel broke the 2024 ceasefire and advanced into Lebanon saying they will silence Hezbollah by the end of the week. Their breath as fire shall devour them.

precepts.text: Herod, in royal apparel, gave an oration and the people shouted, It is the voice of a god; immediately the angel of the Lord smote him because he gave not God the glory, and he was eaten of worms. Our people always think the white man is God; God always reminds them.
precepts.point: He still breathed out fire against the Jews; that hatred is bred in them. Then he fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and said, It is meet to be subject unto God, and a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself as if he were God.
precepts.why:
Cyrus the Persian humbled himself and let all Israel go, and God said, you can rule. But the Greek Antiochus “had spoken proudly”, saying “he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.” As soon as he spoke those proud words, “a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts”, and that most justly, because he had tormented other men’s bowels. He fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and finally said “It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself if he were God.”

It did not stop with the Greeks. Now we come down to the Romans, because that is what Herod was: “And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.”

Black folk always think the white man is God, and God always has to remind you who he is. “And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.” Antiochus rotted with worms rising out of his body; Herod was eaten of worms. The same judgment for the same pride.

Pride destroyed them. All kingdoms fall because of pride, and nobody is exempt: Assyria, Babylon, Greece, Rome, America. That is the judgment for it. So check yourself before you wreck yourself: a man that is mortal must not think of himself as if he were God.

moments.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: The fourth example, and the teacher's favorite: Antiochus came with dishonor out of Persia after being put to flight at Persepolis, heard what had happened to Nicanor, and swelling with anger, thought to avenge upon the Jews the disgrace done unto him. He commanded his chariot to drive without ceasing, the judgment of God now following him, for he had spoken proudly, that he would come to Jerusalem and make it a common burying place of the Jews.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: But the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, smote him with an incurable and invisible plague: a pain of the bowels that was remediless, and sore torments of the inner parts; and that most justly, for he had tormented other men's bowels with many and strange torments. The same things you do to other people, God makes you feel.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Howbeit he nothing at all ceased from his bragging, but still was filled with pride, breathing out fire in his rage against the Jews, and commanding to haste the journey. Everything is going wrong around him and he is still running his mouth. Then he fell down from his chariot, carried violently, so that all the members of his body were much pained.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: And thus he that a little afore thought he might command the waves of the sea, so proud was he beyond the condition of man, and weigh the high mountains in a balance, was now cast on the ground and carried in an horselitter, shewing forth unto all the manifest power of God.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: The worms rose up out of the body of this wicked man; his flesh fell away, and the filthiness of his smell was noisome to all his army, so that no man could endure to carry him for his intolerable stink. The man that thought he could reach to the stars of heaven, nobody could even come near him.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Being plagued, he began to leave off his great pride, and to come to the knowledge of himself by the scourge of God, his pain increasing every moment. He said, It is meet to be subject unto God, and that a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself, as if he were God. Some people get touched once and straighten up; some have to be brought this low to know where they need to go.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: This wicked person vowed unto the Lord, who now no more would have mercy upon him: he promised to set the holy city at liberty, make the Jews equals to the citizens of Athens, garnish the temple with goodly gifts, pay for the sacrifices out of his own revenue, yea, and become a Jew himself, and go through all the world preaching the power of God. When that torment touched him, all of a sudden he wanted to be God's friend.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: But for all this his pains would not cease: for the just judgment of God was come upon him. He wrote the Jews a flattering letter, to the good Jews his citizens, blaming circumstance and commending his son. Thus the murderer and blasphemer, having suffered most grievously, as he entreated other men, so died he a miserable death in a strange country in the mountains. All praises to the Most High God of Israel.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

points: Cyrus humbled himself and let Israel go, so God let him rule. But Antiochus spoke proudly that he would make Jerusalem a common burying place of the Jews, and as soon as he had spoken, the Lord smote him with an incurable and invisible plague in his bowels, a just return for how he had tormented other men's bowels.

He still breathed out fire against the Jews; that hatred is bred in them. Then he fell from his chariot, rotted until he could not abide his own smell, and said, It is meet to be subject unto God, and a man that is mortal should not proudly think of himself as if he were God.
